expectations.text: The output is split into two or more fenced mermaid blocks (by phase or scenario), not one giant diagram
expectations.evidence: 4 diagrams by phase: placement+payment, restaurant acceptance, courier+delivery, notifications.

expectations.text: No single diagram exceeds roughly 25 messages
Participant names/labels are consistent across the diagrams
expectations.evidence: Same id+label pairs across all four (OS as Order Service, K as Kafka, PS as Payment Service, etc.); participant roster listed up front.

expectations.text: Each diagram has its own heading and short introduction, and continuity between diagrams is made explicit
expectations.evidence: Numbered headings with one-paragraph intros; explicit 'Continues from step 9 (approved) of diagram 1' prose plus in-diagram continuity notes.

expectations.text: All described failure branches appear: payment declined -> order FAILED, restaurant reject -> refund + CANCELLED + customer notified, courier decline -> retry with next courier
expectations.evidence: Declined->FAILED (d1) and courier retry loop (d3) are drawn; reject->refund+CANCELLED is drawn (d2), but the prompt-established 'customer notified' on cancellation is never drawn — diagram 2's note defers it to diagram 4, and diagram 4 omits order.cancelled, asking the user instead. The fact of notification was established; only its mechanism was open.

expectations.text: Only widely-supported (safe-core) mermaid syntax is used, since GitHub rendering was requested
expectations.evidence: participants/actors, alt, opt-free, loop, -) async, notes, autonumber; no typed participants, central connections, or other version-gated features.
